messages.author: b431df4437cb4a5f
messages.subject: Error in splinefun(xnew,xx,method="hyman"): zero non-NA points
parts:
Hello- I am fairly new to R and R-INLA but I did perform a search for this error on the discussion board and turned up no results.

I am trying to extract $marginals.fitted.values from a spatial model so that I can create exceedance probabilities. I utilize this bit of code to do so:

MarMarg<-modMarDeath.eco.reg$marginals.fitted.values

MarExc<- sapply(modMarDeath.eco.reg$marginals.fitted.values, 
                FUN = function(MarMarg){1-inla.pmarginal(q=2, marginal = MarMarg)})

but it pitches this error. Error in splinefun(xnew,xx,method="hyman"): zero non-NA points

But I do have "non-NA points" in the list since I can perform it one the first [[1]].
I can upload the full model or list if that would help but I am at a loss on this. It could be something very simple and I am just missing it.

Many thanks,

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error in splinefun(xnew,xx,method="hyman"): zero non-NA points
parts:
sometimes these fitted values could be exp(...) so its >= 0, and then
its harder to get it right close to zero. if you work with the linear
predictor, it seems like you can compute the same MarExc from that one
using that exp(), f.ex (I don't know what it is in your case), is a
monotone function.

like if

fitted = exp(predictor)

then

prob (fitted > 1) = prob(predictor > 0)

Best
H
